dedupe_keys.name: fcc 911 master psap registry public safety answering points united states

description: The 911 Master PSAP Registry is the Federal Communications Commission's list of public safety answering points, the call centres that receive 911 calls in the United States. The producer is the FCC Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau, which assigns each PSAP an identification number used in carrier filings. Coverage is national: 8,557 rows across 55 state and territory values. Each row gives the PSAP ID, name, county, city and state, the type of the last record change and its date, and a city-level geocode. The table is available on the FCC open data portal for download as CSV or JSON, through the Socrata API, and as a map locator; it is free and in the public domain as a U.S. Government work. Caveats: the rows were last updated in October 2017 while the description says the registry was current in February 2019, so consolidations since then are missing; the geocode is only at city level and missing for some rows; the table lists centres but not their staffing, call volumes or backup arrangements, and the FCC's current registry on fcc.gov could not be read from this environment. Simulation uses: mapping which call centre serves an area, modelling the load shifted to neighbouring PSAPs when one fails or its telecom links go down, and siting studies for dispatch capacity. Related records: the NYC 911 end-to-end response times (data-nyc-911-end-to-end-response-times) show operations at one large PSAP, and the FCC DIRS disaster reports, catalogued by the digital piece, record PSAP outages during disasters.
